title: Staffage cast manifest
description: Named, figure-only renderings of the staffage archive: one entry per cast id, either a pose (one frame, or a transient thermal timeline) or a clip (one frame per scheduled time).

FlowLayer.description: A layer of the thermodynamic flow view, the one vocabulary of drawn air: streams (stream lines of the instant with arrow heads, coloured by the temperature excess of the air), tracers (particles advected along the streams), moisture (vapour clouds and dotted vapour lines), fog (condensed droplets where the mixture is below its dew point) and pathlines (the path each parcel actually travelled, the honest picture of unsteady flow such as breath).

LodId.description: A level of detail of the cast levels file.

LodRevision.description: Eight lower-case hex digits of the canonical-JSON hash of a resolved level.

Revision.description: A content hash: sha256 and 64 lower-case hex digits.

Provenance.description: Where one rendered cast came from, in every dimension the contract names (T/r3-contract.md). The exporter writes it, the Python loader checks it against the manifest entry and the catalog, scenes read it.

clock.description: The clock of the frames. offsetS is the clip time of frame 0 and always 0: the history of the air (flowDevelopS) lies before the frames and never shifts them. rate is not known to the exporter: a scene adds it (staffage_provenance with a rate, or a staffage_motion).

lod.description: The level of detail the frames were drawn at (T/STAFFAGE-LOD-DESIGN.md): the level id and the revision of its resolved parameters.

flow.description: The layers of the flow view drawn over the figure, in the order of the cast entry; empty for a cast without drawn air.
The layers of the flow view drawn over the figure, in the order of the cast entry; empty for a cast without drawn air.

Structure.description: The structural summary of a forces or moments cast: one entry per frame position in the frame order, in newtons and newton-metres at the world positions the frames use (x ahead, y up, z left; a mirrored cast has x and the y and z components of moments negated). Compression is negative axial force. A moment is a moment of force, never a momentum.

Logical.description: The physical truth of a cast, identical for every level of detail: the figure height in metres over the canonical clock, the paper extent of the figure in world metres (feet origin; the rig bounds in the side elevation, the drawn shapes of the front and plan), the polygons of frame 0 by shape id in world metres, and the most paths any frame draws.

Index.description: The index the exporter writes next to the frames of one cast.

lod.description: How the level sampled the canonical clock: fps is the effective rate of the sampled frames, canonicalFrames and canonicalFps those of the full level.

Cast.description: One cast. Give exactly one of pose and clip. fps needs a clip or a timeline. environment, timeline, thermalSpanK and flow exist for the thermal view only; environment and timeline exclude each other. flow needs flowDevelopS; flowTrailS, flowStrokeMm and flowSpacingMm need flow, flowTrailS the pathlines layer. A cast has no language: it renders figure-only (no text), so its output is the same for every language.

theme.description: The ink and palette of the analytic views (thermal, forces, moments); required, no default. Line and solid views carry their theme in the view name.

flow.description: The layers of the thermodynamic flow view drawn over the figure (the air of breath, plumes, jets, steam); figure-only, so no legends and no labels.

flowDevelopS.description: Flow layers only, required with them, never defaulted: the seconds the air has developed before every frame. The flow of a frame is solved that many seconds after the frame's own time and no parcel lives longer, so frame 0 already shows the developed field instead of empty air. A looping clip moves on by whole periods, so pose and breath stay in phase, the field is periodic with the clip and the loop closes without a jump (the period is derived, never authored); a pose keeps its instant; a clip that does not loop shows the air this many seconds ahead of its figure, so keep it short against the changes of such a clip.

flowTrailS.description: The pathlines layer only. Seconds of each path's recent travel that stay visible: the line fades towards its tail, so breath reads as a dispersing puff instead of a bundle anchored at the nose; absent: the whole path from the emission at full strength.

flowStrokeMm.description: Flow layers only. Paper width of the widest stream in millimetres at the cast scale; every line of the flow (streams, tracers, vapour lines, paths) scales with it. Absent: 0.3 mm, the hairlines of a print, which vanish when the figure plays at a few hundred pixels.

flowSpacingMm.description: Flow layers only. The smallest paper distance in millimetres between two drawn streams, puffs or paths at the cast scale (the generalisation of the flow marks); the level of detail multiplies it by its flowSpacingFactor. Absent: 2.2 mm.

scale.description: The authored scale variant, required, no default: a preset denominator at which the asset holds an authored representation (the exporter refuses unavailable and derived scales).

fps.description: Frames per second of a clip or timeline; required for both, forbidden for a still pose. A schedule of more than 600 frames is thinned to 600 evenly spaced samples, so the exported index fps may be fractional; play such a cast with a rate in the scene.

timeline.description: A transient environment: preset slugs keyed by absolute time in seconds, strictly increasing.

thermalSpanK.description: Thermal view only. A symmetric surface-temperature range of plus and minus this many kelvin around the air temperature of the cast environment (the legend states it). Absent: the absolute shared range of -20 to 60 degC. The course casts use 25 K, one value for all thermal casts that are on screen together (one Scene class) so they stay comparable; the guard test thermal_span checks it.

mirror.description: Flip the figure about the vertical axis of the world origin; the index bounds are mirrored with it.
